summary: A first-person commuter essay on the first-mile/last-mile (FMLM) problem of getting between home and transit stations. It follows the city's October 15, 2023 plan to deploy electric shuttle buses with a real-time tracking app, funded partly through public-private partnerships. By early November the shuttles have improved the author's commute, community feeling and accessibility, though glitches remain and the city council is weighing where to expand next.
one_line: A commuter describes how the city's new electric FMLM shuttle program, with a tracking app and private partners, eased commuting and improved accessibility.
key_facts: The author's narrative begins on Monday, September 4, 2023, when the author describes daily commuting struggles with the first-mile/last-mile (FMLM) challenge.
The author's nearest subway station is a mile and a half from home, requiring walking or costly ride-sharing in bad weather.
On October 15, 2023, the city's transportation department unveiled a plan to improve FMLM connections.
Transportation Commissioner Sandra Nguyen spearheaded the initiative to deploy a fleet of electric shuttle buses circulating through neighborhoods to major transit hubs.
The program includes a smart app that tracks the shuttles in real time.
The city partnered with several tech companies, including ride-sharing company GoRide Tech, to fund the program.
GoRide Tech CEO David Thompson said public-private partnerships help 'build a more connected and sustainable city.'
By early November the shuttles had been operating for a few weeks, and the author's shuttle arrives within a few minutes of leaving home and is shared with a handful of neighbors.
Commuter Michael Zhang said, 'It's changed the way I view public transit. I feel more connected to my city than ever before.'
The service has improved accessibility for the elderly, people with disabilities, and parents with young children.
Occasional delays and technical glitches remain, and more areas still need coverage.

At the November 29 city council meeting, council member Jason Rodriguez led discussions on evaluating FMLM services to decide where to expand next, with metrics showing increased ridership and satisfaction.
